original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-zariski-descent-effective}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $S = \bigcup U_i$ be an open covering.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for the family $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is
effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $S = \bigcup U_i$ be an open covering.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for the family $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is
effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
hypotheses: S is a scheme.
{U_i⊂S} is an open cover.
A quasi-coherent descent datum consists of sheaves F_i on S_i with pairwise pullback isomorphisms satisfying the triple cocycle condition.
conclusions: Each descent datum for {U_i→S} arises from a quasi-coherent sheaf on S.
The canonical functor QCoh(S)→Desc({U_i→S}) is fully faithful.
semantic_review_note: Effectivity (essential surjectivity) and full faithfulness are separate assertions that together give equivalence; the descent datum is sheaf gluing with cocycle, not arbitrary presheaf data.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descent-datum-cosimplicial}
Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Given a descent datum $(N, \varphi)$ we can associate to it a
cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module $N_\bullet$\footnote{We should really
write $(N, \varphi)_\bullet$.} by the
rules $N_n = N_{n, n}$ and given $\beta : [n] \to [m]$
setting we define
$$
N_\bullet(\beta) = (\varphi^m_{\beta(n)m}) \circ N_{\beta, n} :
N_{n, n} \longrightarrow N_{m, m}.
$$
This procedure is functorial in the descent datum.
statement:
Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Given a descent datum $(N, \varphi)$ we can associate to it a
cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module $N_\bullet$\footnote{We should really
write $(N, \varphi)_\bullet$.} by the
rules $N_n = N_{n, n}$ and given $\beta : [n] \to [m]$
setting we define
$$
N_\bullet(\beta) = (\varphi^m_{\beta(n)m}) \circ N_{\beta, n} :
N_{n, n} \longrightarrow N_{m, m}.
$$
This procedure is functorial in the descent datum.
hypotheses: R→A is a ring homomorphism.
(N,φ) is an A-module descent datum relative to R→A.
(A/R)_n=A^{⊗_R(n+1)}, and N_{n,i}, φ^n_{ij}, N_{β,n} are the constructions immediately before the lemma.
conclusions: There is a cosimplicial (A/R)_•-module N_• with N_n=N_{n,n} and N_•(β)=φ^m_{β(n),m}∘N_{β,n} for each monotone β:[n]→[m].
This assignment is functorial in morphisms of descent data.
semantic_review_note: Both cosimplicial construction and functoriality asserted, with n-dependent factor placement preserved and no assumption that β is injective.

Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module. The cosimplicial

Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module. The cosimplicial
$(A/R)_\bullet$-module associated to the canonical descent

hypotheses: R→A is a ring map.

(A⊗_R M,can) is the canonical descent datum.
conclusions: The associated cosimplicial (A/R)_•-module is isomorphic to (A/R)_•⊗_R M.

Suppose that $R \to A$ has a section.
Then for any $R$-module $M$ the extended cochain complex
(\ref{equation-extended-complex}) is exact.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-recognize-effective}
Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map.
Let $(N, \varphi)$ be a descent datum.
Then $(N, \varphi)$ is effective if and only if the canonical
map
$$
A \otimes_R H^0(s(N_\bullet)) \longrightarrow N
$$
is an isomorphism.

Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map.
Let $(N, \varphi)$ be a descent datum.
Then $(N, \varphi)$ is effective if and only if the canonical
map
$$
A \otimes_R H^0(s(N_\bullet)) \longrightarrow N
$$
is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: R→A is faithfully flat.
(N,φ) is a module descent datum for R→A.
N_• is the associated cosimplicial (A/R)_•-module.
conclusions: The descent datum (N,φ) is effective if and only if the natural A-linear map A⊗_R H^0(s(N_•))→N is an isomorphism.
equivalence_sides: The descent datum (N,φ) is effective if and only if the natural A-linear map A⊗_R H^0(s(N_•))→N is an isomorphism.
semantic_review_note: This is a biconditional comparing effectivity to a canonical isomorphism, not an assumed effectivity condition.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descent-descends}
Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map, and let $R \to R'$
be faithfully flat. Set $A' = R' \otimes_R A$. If all descent data
for $R' \to A'$ are effective, then so are all descent data for $R \to A$.
statement:
Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map, and let $R \to R'$
be faithfully flat. Set $A' = R' \otimes_R A$. If all descent data
for $R' \to A'$ are effective, then so are all descent data for $R \to A$.
hypotheses: R→A and R→R' are faithfully flat ring maps.
A'=R'⊗_R A.
Every module descent datum for R'→A' is effective.
conclusions: Every module descent datum for R→A is effective.
semantic_review_note: Corrects potential confusion between two faithfully flat maps and a base change: all effectiveness is assumed only after R→R'; original R→A effectiveness follows.

\label{lemma-standard-fpqc-covering}
Let $S$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to S\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
be a standard fpqc covering of $S$, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-standard-fpqc}.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
statement:
Let $S$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to S\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
be a standard fpqc covering of $S$, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-standard-fpqc}.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
hypotheses: S is an affine scheme.
U={U_i→S}_{i=1..n} is a finite standard fpqc covering.
Descent data consist of quasi-coherent sheaves F_i on U_i with cocycle isomorphisms on overlaps.
conclusions: All quasi-coherent descent data for U are effective.
QCoh(S)→Desc_QCoh(U) is fully faithful.
semantic_review_note: Keep both effectiveness and full faithfulness for finite standard fpqc covering; standard affines flat with joint surjectivity, no extra finite-presentation condition.
